summary: RequestContext.Create(string correlationId) and RequestContext.CreateForTest read DateTimeOffset.UtcNow directly instead of TimeProvider, unlike the parameterless Create() in the same file (line 66) which correctly uses TimeProvider.System.GetUtcNow(); both are public API so callers cannot inject a TimeProvider for these paths.

No test builds the ServiceProvider produced by the core AddEncina() with ValidateOnBuild=true and ValidateScopes=true and resolves every registered service, so a future registration gap (as in #1260/#1273/#1285/#1289) would not be caught for the mediator itself.

AddApplicationMessaging (two overloads) is documented as a 'Legacy alias for AddEncina', a compatibility alias kept without [Obsolete], contradicting the project's 'No Legacy Code' / 'No Migration Paths' rule for a pre-1.0 codebase with no external users to migrate.
proposed_destination: backlog (remove or justify; maintainer decision needed since removing a public API is a breaking change even pre-1.0)

summary: The manifest's reason field for Core/EncinaConfiguration.cs reads 'EF entity type configuration', which describes an unrelated class shape (EF Core entity configuration classes); EncinaConfiguration.cs is actually the mediator's fluent registration configuration (RegisterServicesFromAssemblies, AddPipelineBehavior, etc.) and has nothing to do with EF Core.

The manifest declares only unit for Core/EncinaConfiguration.cs, but tests/Encina.GuardTests/Core/EncinaConfigurationGuardTests.cs exists, passes, and exercises 71.1% of the file's lines (measured), so guard should also be listed as an applicable flag.

The XML remarks say 'This is the default strategy and maintains backward compatibility with existing behavior', language that assumes a compatibility concern the pre-1.0 philosophy explicitly disclaims; it is stale wording, not a functional issue.
